```html Construction Points from Architect's Specs
CONSTRUCTION POINTS FROM ARCHITECT'S SPECS
Specifications for House of the Month
(Continued from page 34)

ings for cellar columns and piers shall be no less than 12" x 24" x 24".

WALLS:

Foundation walls shall be built of 12" concrete blocks below grade as per Building Code with 8" blocks above grade, or poured concrete with joints of portland cement mortar. Interior and exterior of sill foundation walls to receive 2 coats of cement mortar parge. All concrete walls above to be 8" cement blocks carried to height as shown on plans and given a coat of cement on all surfaces. Beam pockets and anchor bolt holes projecting to be put on exterior walls below grade.

CHIMNEY:

Build chimney of stone and brick as per specifications, details, and sections as shown in cellar and provide metal thimble for same. Build in 4½" Covert Bipost and damper and ash door with heavy cover. Special care should be given the lining in all flues. Chimney clean-out doors, thimbles, etc. Draughts or chimney to be tested by Architect with approved smoke standard tools. Detail of fireplace will be submitted by Architect.

CONCRETE FLOORS:

Cellar floor shall be 1 part cement, 2 parts sand, and 5 parts cinders and topped with 1" portland cement mixed 1 part cement, 2 parts sand smooth and even and pitched to trap pit.

DRAIN PIPES:

Lay 4" earthenware drain pipes from cellar floor connection to main catch or dry wells or from house. These pipes shall be independent of sewer or other drain pipes and shall be laid with proper grade to prevent water from underside of same. Put in floor drains in cellar at boiler and in garage and run to stone dry wells. All drain work to be executed in an approved manner under supervision of Architect, to earthenware drain tile to be laid around footings. Good agricultural tile to be used for outlets to gravel.

BULKHEADS:

Provide and set C. I. concrete filled columns 4" in diameter in cellar for support of wood girder. Columns shall be set immediately after the parging on place, and shall rest on concrete footings.

CINDER CONCRETE:

In bathrooms prepare floor with cinder concrete grouted and to within 1½" of finish floor. Provide proper pitches to drains.

LATHING AND PLASTERING:

Lath all walls and ceilings, cellar, and walls between through cellar, ceilings and walls, driving rooms, through ceilings, attic, etc., with black herringbone rib lath, furring posts, nail scratch and brown coat with wood fiber; metal corners; cover all finish and approved hydrated lime, gauged with plaster of Paris on all plumb, even and carefully trowelled to a fine, smooth finish. Metal beads is to be used at all angles and arched openings.

CEILING:

Contractor shall grade premises around house to secure good drainage away from and finish same with 6" bluestone, 3'0" wide flagstone base sills from driveway to front steps. Terrace steps with flag treads and bluestone risers to be finished with colored flagstone well cemented down.

SIDING:

Contractor to use white pine lumber.

TIMBER:

All timber shall be of sound, full dimensioned wane or fir, free from defects, large loose or unsound knots, or shakes.

FRAMING:

Set all timbers in the usual manner for convenient to building in accordance with drawings and details and as hereinafter specified, shall extend from sill to plate and ribbon strip or girth shall be notched into studs at proper height and securely spiked; solid blocking shall be placed at corners and shall be embedded in cement on the wall. Ends of floor beams shall be placed under outside walls and securely spiked or bolted thereto. Floor beams shall be doubled under all partitions running the same way, and also for trimmers around stair wells and for all headers and other openings. The tail beams and headers shall rest on 2" x 4" strips on wall spiked to the furring blocks, floor beams shall be leveled, and bridged out over and well spiked to the header. Spiking ends to be cut from strip at full beams to headers and braces to receive same.

SIZES:

Sills 4" x 6", corner posts and intermediate posts 4" x 4", plates, studs or girts 2" x 4", roof rafters 2" x 6"—16" o. c., end and attic tier of beams, 2" x 8"—16" o. c., and 1st 2nd floor joists 2" x 8"—16" o. c. Doubled studding and lintels 2" x 8", hip ridge 2" x 8", girder in cellar 6" x 8" yellow pine or Mahogany.

BRIDGING:

All floor beams at 7 ft. centers shall be bridged with 1½" x 2" herringbone bridging double nailed at each end; Bridging shall be put in between pieces of floor beams and well nailed.

STUDDING:

Studding shall be double at each window, doors, and other openings, bearing partitions and back plastered. Backing for wall plates. Wherever practical the studs shall extend through the height of the floor beams and rest on bottom plate; securely spike to plate, top, bottom, and girder to insure best cracks from shrinkage. Wide openings shall have 2—2" x 8" heads with bridging between.

The stair contractor shall take measurements of and not nailed in between same; corners of all intersecting partitions shall in all cases be made strong and secure with 4" x 6" built-up double braces, which shall extend over no less than 10" grade studs on outside walls.

SHEATHING:

Sheathing on outside walls shall be enclosed with 1" x 10" N. C. boards dressed one side, shiplap, put on horizontally and securely nailed to all studs. Outside walls to be covered either with a heavy building paper or singerly tarpaper, which will allow for wall being enclosed. All floors to be laid with 1" x 6" T. & G. pine sub floor neatly matched and securely nailed according to drawings and rafters with 1" x 2" shingle lath well nailed and even. Shingle and boards to be stored in the dry from weather. Weatherbest or Creodipt stained shingles laid 5½"— to the weather. Order of shingles by Architect.

FRAMES & SASH:

All window sash shall be of stock size as detailed on plans except for special sizes specified. Double hung sash to be 1⅜". All sash to be hung with Samson Spot Sash Cord.

SCREENS:

Screens to be applied on all windows and door openings. Porch to be screened in with entrance doors as located by owner. All screens to be copper wire or bronze if located on EXTERIOR. Exterior of building to be sheathed and covered with black building paper, and to be properly covered with cypress clapboards applied over exterior and laid in pattern as directed by owner. Cedar of shingles to be selected by Architect.

GLASS:

All glass to be bedded in putty except where new provided shall be as specified. Sizes as per drawings. Where required, glass to be double thick American sheet glass, clear, straight, and free from blisters and minor scratches. Under direction and to satisfaction by the Owner, Contractor shall clean all glass and paint sashes, etc., and replace all broken and defective glass before final payment will be made and order.

EXTERIOR TRIM:

All exterior trim, such as water-table, posts, boards, etc., shall be of cypress. Underside of main cornice projections shall be rolled with 5/8" x 6" T. & G. box boards nailed to rafters with ten-penny wire nails.

DOOR FRAMES:

Exterior door frames shall be 1⅜" outside casing and 2" sills.

INTERIOR:

Interior door framing shall be 1x6 at and 2nd story and in attic, on which by a 5⁄8" x 2½" straight grained white oak floor base. Floor beams shall be 2" x 8" yellow pine or N. C. 1" x 4" G., and R. N. At the intersection of studs and base provide and put down stock floor beams at their height at proper intervals between rough and finished flooring. Cut in deafening between beams in bathrooms and plastered ceilings. No stud shall be cut without permission from Architect. All cross-bridging to be sandpapered. Scraping of floors shall be deferred until the very last end at work being done or finished in all details, including baseboard, quarter strip oak border on floors in living room, dining room and master bedroom. Linoleum on kitchen floor to be selected by Owner.

TRIM AND BASE:

Trim throughout the house shall be 5⁄8" x 4½" ―stop, this will include all jambs. Build backs from floor to studs to floor with base blocks. All trim in living room, dining room, library, and hall to be chestnut. Base in master bedroom and den to be Cypress, balance to suit. Closet base 7½" high without moulding. Window sill door openings shall be 7⁄8" x 1½". recky cypress; balance pine to be selected by Owner, in kitchen. Rockcases, dining room cabinet and living room paneled waincecoting to be as shown on plans in the library are to be of chestnut.

WEATHER STRIPPING:

All exterior doors and windows to be weather-stripped.

FLOORS:

Provide and install wood floors in cellar.

INSULATION:

All exterior walls and attic floor beams to be insulated with 4" mineral wool insulation; to fill all stud spaces, beams and floor spaces or voids between packings.

JAMBS AND HEADS:

All jambs and heads for inside doors shall be 7⁄8" x 4½" N. C. yellow pine as required

DOORS:

Doors shall be of sizes on drawings, shall be six panel moulded white pine standard or Birch veneer doors. In rooms where chestnut trim might be used, doors in be of similar material. Front door shall be 1¾" and rear and exterior doors 1¾" of cypress or white pine. Include 1 panel door about 18" x 5'6" for bathrooms, pantry cupboard and closet doors, shall be moulded saddles of oak same as floors.

CLOSETS:

All closets shall have on 1st floor, shelf and pole at proper height, and on 2nd floor, five 12" shelves. Any special closets shall be built as per detail by architect or "Morgan Millwork" Company.

STAIRS:

Cellar stairs shall be 1½" strings, 1⅛" x 9", treads and necessary handrails, all of yellow pine. Second floor stairs shall be 1¼" string planks, 1⅛" treads ⅞" risers with moulded nosing, newels, platforms, atc., all of chestnut wood. Attic stairs shall be 1⅛" string ⅞" rail, which shall be of wrought iron. Stairs shall be properly housed, wedged and glued. The stair contractor shall be responsible for providing necessary carriage timbers and furring for lath ing.

well-hole and head room and shall submit layout of all staircases to Architect before building same for approval.

HARDWARE:

The carpenter shall provide all hardware such as nails, screws, spikes, besides bolts, anchors, joist hangers, etc. All hardware and application of finished hardware of hammered wrought type. Hardware to be selected by owner. All window sash to be hung with Samson Spot Sash Cord.

DRESSERS:

Dressers in kitchen and pantry shall be placed with swinging sash doors, shelves, drawers as shown. Hinged doors, plate strip and shall extends to ceiling.

MEDICINE CABINET:

Provide and set in bathroom with two shelves and bevel edge mirror as shown. Cabinet to be about 21" x 7" in size, 5" deep with bevel edged mirror in door.

WINDOW SHUTTERS:

Window shutters to be applied where not built in detail shown on drawings.

CUTTING:

Do all necessary cutting for all trades and do all small clean for plumber, steamfitter, electrician, etc. No charge except for building all rubbish except that of the mason and larger the building known about.

SCAFFOLDING:

Carpenter to provide all necessary scaffolding for mason.

PAINTING & EXTERIOR:

All exterior woodwork to receive three coats of best quality white lead and oil paint, mixed as per Building Code, all holes puttied, and shall be painted 3 coats of shingle stain. All clapboards and pure white paint to be selected by owner.

INTERIOR:

All interior woodwork shall be stained with an oil stain, all nail holes puttied before giving the following: All trim to be varnished: make of varnish or at option of Owner, interior woodwork to be painted three coats of lead and oil paint with a coat of stippled paint. All closets, attic to be well sandpapered and cleaned before the first coat is applied. All inside walls to be painted with Texolite. All ceilings 2 coats of Muresco. All work to have finished coat of enamel. Any textured plaster to be painted and stippled. Walls white-washered twice, floors sanded twice, and all mill work to be sand-papered smooth [?] for copper throughout for all the flashings. Finish the sides of the chimney where it intersects with the house on both sides with straight tooth. Flash over all window heads, sides of windows, intertions of porches, and extensions of all projecting walls.

Gutters and leaders to be copper as above. Gutters to be ½" round 5" wide and properly held in proper grade and leaders 3" round corrugated and tight.

Provide the necessary sleeves and collars to be set to be built in ceilings. All gutters to have the proper pitch to leaders.

All leaders to be 3½" round corrugated or square with connection to cistern or dry well.

Provide copper wire baskets at all leader openings to the gutters.

KITCHEN SINK:

Kitchen with 4'6" above floor to be prepared with wire lath and scratched with cement plaster, to receive 4" x 4" tile. Bathroom walls to be prepared same and to receive one inch hexagonal or square ceramic tile with cemented border. Sanitary cove and base in bath room and shower. All tiles furnished by Hearths to receive 4" x ¼" quarry tile of colors to be selected by the Owners. The in master bathroom [?] all tile work and colors to be selected by Owner. Bathroom accessories to consist of the following and shall be built-in with tile work: Glass shelf and soap dish over wash holder, 1 shelf over toilet, 1 tooth brush holder, and 2 large towel holders.

All the work to be liberally buttered and at complete variance with written consent and thoroughly set in cement.

PLUMBING, GENERAL:

The plumbing shall be done in the best manner employing with all existing laws and ordinances. All work to be of best material and workmanship, all pipes tested, no clay pipe joints permitted, all piping shall be properly pitched for draining, sewage drains to be of cast iron, and soil and vent piping to be of cast iron or black brass throughout, provided with necessary traps and other fittings. All fixture to be of standard pattern of approved make selected by Owner. House sewer shall be earthenware or stone ware pipe and shall be by wiped joint to house drain.

Contractor shall provide separate soil pipe and vent and waste line of standard galvanized iron and all short branches to waste and soil and vent. All necessary sleeves and collars of roof to be used for caulking, and connections between lead roof and soil line be wiped joints and between floors soldered joints and made tight. Leader and horizontal runs shall have no less fall than ¼" per foot. Use [?] cast and 45 degree elbows for drainage changes of direction and 60 and 90 degree Y, all properly fastened and supported.

SEPTIC TANK:

The plumber will make a septic tank consisting of 40 feet of 4" earthenware pipe, which shall be continued to within 100 feet of the house line where it shall be screened and connected in standard clay tile to tank shall be 500 gallon capacity built of concrete as manufactured by the Standard Products Company.

HOUSE DRAIN, ETC.:

House drain shall be made of pipe, terra, and 4" x 4" shall be placed in bottom of footing drain, sewer to house, and inlet, place in house side of trap and carried to outside with a cast iron perforated plate in wall. All leaders to be piped to blind drain.

THE AMERICAN BUILDER HOUSE OF THE MONTH
```
